item.text: {"chapter_id":"8B","draft":{"chapter_id":"8B","answers":[{"question_id":"8B.1","answer":"The shards indicate a mostly explicit but internally tensioned program: austerity and anti-corruption, poverty reduction and social transfers, state-led infrastructure and development, energy and food self-sufficiency, pacification and security reform, expanded military roles, and institutional change. The program appears in campaign platforms, plans, speeches, budgets, laws, and formal strategies, but no single dated portfolio fully fixes priorities or resolves conflicts such as demilitarization versus militarization.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0051-E011","BATCH-0051-E012","BATCH-0037-E003","BATCH-0024-E001","BATCH-0055-E002","BATCH-0055-E015"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0038-E006","BATCH-0026-E010","BATCH-0051-E023","BATCH-0052-E002"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The complete hierarchy of goals and their status in 2023 is unresolved.","Some goals are attributed to the administration or institutions rather than personally to López Obrador."]},{"question_id":"8B.2","answer":"Major priorities were translated into budgets, laws, institutions, operating rules, appointments, programs, infrastructure, and security arrangements, including social-program machinery, health federalization, labor and pension reforms, National Guard structures, military administration of infrastructure, and energy measures. Translation was uneven: some measures remained proposals, lacked clear objectives or controls, were legally constrained or invalidated, or were not demonstrably directed by the president.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E002","BATCH-0050-E004","BATCH-0051-E001","BATCH-0051-E002","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0026-E014","BATCH-0055-E003","BATCH-0055-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E014","BATCH-0051-E013","BATCH-0051-E023","BATCH-0055-E006","BATCH-0055-E008","BATCH-0030-E005"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Formal architecture does not establish completed execution.","Personal ownership is incomplete for legislation, agency decisions, and subnational implementation."]},{"question_id":"8B.3","answer":"The administration mobilized substantial financial, administrative, social, and military resources toward selected priorities. Evidence includes expanded social-program budgets and field networks, health-system structures, infrastructure and state-enterprise activity, and expanded military and National Guard roles. Mobilization was broad but uneven: austerity, centralization, procurement and monitoring weaknesses, civilian-capacity losses, and resource displacement limited effective use, while several activities depended on agencies, subnational governments, partners, or the military.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E002","BATCH-0051-E015","BATCH-0051-E016","BATCH-0041-E002","BATCH-0055-E007","BATCH-0026-E005","BATCH-0032-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E009","BATCH-0051-E019","BATCH-0047-E013","BATCH-0030-E011","BATCH-0052-E020"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Resource allocation and staffing do not by themselves establish effective mobilization.","Direct presidential command and whole-portfolio mobilization are not comprehensively documented."]},{"question_id":"8B.4","answer":"Personnel management shows some active selection, empowerment, training, and replacement, including senior appointments, agency changes, social-program staffing, health supervisory structures, and National Guard recruitment and training. But the evidence does not establish systematic competence across the portfolio. It also records delayed appointments, staffing shortages, institutional dysfunction, military assignment to civilian functions, and concerns that loyalty or political alignment displaced expertise; individual presidential attribution is often unclear.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0039-E001","BATCH-0044-E005","BATCH-0050-E002","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0055-E009","BATCH-0055-E010"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0051-E019","BATCH-0048-E015","BATCH-0055-E008","BATCH-0047-E010","BATCH-0026-E006"],"limitations_and_gaps":["There is no comprehensive roster linking appointment decisions to performance.","Formal training and institutional roles do not prove capable execution."]},{"question_id":"8B.5","answer":"Coordination and territorial reach were substantial in selected social, health, infrastructure, security, party, and emergency systems, with prescribed reporting, regional structures, interagency mechanisms, and nationwide deployments. Follow-through was inconsistent: service coverage and local capacity varied, registries and archives were incomplete, autonomous and forensic bodies were impaired, institutional resistance persisted, and several coordination mechanisms were documented only as formal arrangements rather than verified compliance.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0051-E002","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0052-E015","BATCH-0055-E004","BATCH-0057-E003","BATCH-0029-E007","BATCH-0013-E001"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E015","BATCH-0049-E005","BATCH-0031-E019","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0057-E001"],"limitations_and_gaps":["There is no comprehensive ministry-by-ministry or territorial compliance dataset.","Some favorable coordination was partner-led or institutionally collective rather than presidentially attributable."]},{"question_id":"8B.6","answer":"Many priorities became observable practice: transfers and pensions were delivered at scale, labor and tax measures operated, health and social systems issued rules, security and infrastructure functions were performed, and major projects advanced. Implementation remained mixed, with medication and health-access problems, weak results measurement, incomplete or costly infrastructure, environmental and legal disputes, cancelled or scaled-down projects, persistent impunity, and invalidated institutional provisions.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E002","BATCH-0050-E004","BATCH-0051-E002","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0052-E016","BATCH-0055-E003","BATCH-0044-E011","BATCH-0031-E008"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E005","BATCH-0050-E015","BATCH-0048-E009","BATCH-0030-E004","BATCH-0031-E013","BATCH-0055-E006"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Launches, formal rules, and outputs do not establish service quality or durable operation.","Evidence is sectoral and often cumulative or joint-government rather than ruler-specific."]},{"question_id":"8B.7","answer":"Results moved in different directions across the program. Social transfers, wage policy, poverty measures, pension reach, and some income or inclusion indicators improved, while health access, medicine availability, education, extreme poverty, regional inequality, violence, impunity, security capacity, energy performance, and some infrastructure indicators remained adverse or unresolved. Attribution is limited by pandemic recovery, remittances, wage changes, inherited conditions, criminal actors, subnational action, external trends, and lagged measures.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E002","BATCH-0032-E004","BATCH-0050-E003","BATCH-0050-E004","BATCH-0051-E013","BATCH-0052-E016","BATCH-0054-E003"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E003","BATCH-0050-E005","BATCH-0051-E014","BATCH-0051-E017","BATCH-0048-E012","BATCH-0055-E017"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most outcome evidence ends before or near the end of 2023.","No complete frozen-goal baseline or counterfactual isolates presidential contribution across the portfolio."]},{"question_id":"8B.8","answer":"Some adaptation is documented through program redesign, institutional transitions, route and personnel changes, revised results frameworks, monitoring systems, emergency mechanisms, and changed lending or implementation arrangements. However, the evidence rarely shows a direct audit-to-presidential-decision chain. Recommendations were sometimes disregarded, indicators and controls remained weak, failures persisted, and militarization or contested approaches continued despite adverse evidence.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0051-E003","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0044-E005","BATCH-0052-E020","BATCH-0054-E005","BATCH-0057-E017"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0051-E023","BATCH-0052-E002","BATCH-0050-E015","BATCH-0055-E008","BATCH-0030-E011"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Agency, partner, or court-driven adaptation cannot be assumed to show presidential learning.","Replacement and redesign are not consistently linked to diagnosed failure or improved results."]},{"question_id":"8B.9","answer":"Crisis and resistance responses preserved some priorities through social and financial stabilization, emergency mobilization, infrastructure and security continuation, legal strategies, and expanded institutional arrangements. They were nevertheless mixed: courts constrained or invalidated major measures, the Culiacán operation failed, disaster recovery and protection were incomplete, health-transition problems persisted, military and security responses remained contested, and institutional resistance or noncooperation was not consistently overcome. Allegations and advocacy claims remain qualified rather than findings of personal intent.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0052-E015","BATCH-0052-E025","BATCH-0050-E010","BATCH-0052-E010","BATCH-0055-E002","BATCH-0044-E009","BATCH-0029-E003"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0055-E006","BATCH-0055-E008","BATCH-0016-E004","BATCH-0031-E003","BATCH-0047-E013","BATCH-0051-E020"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Several responses were substantially implemented by other institutions or external actors.","Long-term recovery, legal consequences, and international outcomes remain incompletely observed."]},{"question_id":"8B.10","answer":"By the period end, substantial parts of the program had become budgets, transfer systems, operating rules, labor and pension measures, military and National Guard roles, administrative structures, and major infrastructure commitments. The conversion was not broad or securely durable: health and education capacity weakened, security and energy objectives remained unresolved, projects had cost, environmental, legal, or operational weaknesses, measurement and oversight were deficient, and some institutional changes were invalidated or dependent on personal and military control. Long-term durability and successor-period effects remain open.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E004","BATCH-0051-E001","BATCH-0051-E002","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0052-E014","BATCH-0052-E016","BATCH-0055-E003","BATCH-0049-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E005","BATCH-0051-E014","BATCH-0051-E017","BATCH-0052-E020","BATCH-0055-E006","BATCH-0055-E008","BATCH-0030-E005"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The end-period record does not cover every material program component.","Durability beyond 2023, fiscal sustainability, and ruler-attributable outcomes remain unresolved."]}],"cross_lens_observations":["The common pattern is substantial formalization and selective delivery alongside uneven coordination, weak measurement, mixed outcomes, and limited evidence of personally directed adaptation.","The evidence base is concentrated in social policy, health, infrastructure, security, militarization, transparency, and selected crisis cases; citation volume does not establish whole-portfolio effectiveness.","Moral approval or disapproval of the program is excluded from these execution judgments."]},"critique":{"chapter_id":"8B","issues":[{"question_id":"8B.1","issue_type":"misleading_weight","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0051-E011","BATCH-0051-E012","BATCH-0037-E003","BATCH-0055-E002"],"explanation":"The shard drafts sometimes treat repeated rhetoric and retrospective summaries as equivalent to a dated, frozen program. These establish declared themes but not necessarily operational hierarchy, persistence, or personal ownership."},{"question_id":"8B.2","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0055-E007","BATCH-0041-E002"],"explanation":"Formal laws, budgets, and institutional designs support operationalization, but not completion or personally directed execution of every measure."},{"question_id":"8B.3","issue_type":"misleading_weight","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E002","BATCH-0055-E007","BATCH-0032-E006"],"explanation":"Budget, staffing, and military-role evidence demonstrates mobilization, not effectiveness; administrative and military activity is overrepresented relative to the full program."},{"question_id":"8B.4","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0039-E001","BATCH-0044-E005","BATCH-0055-E009"],"explanation":"Named appointments, training, and replacement show personnel action but do not establish capability, selection motive, or improved execution."},{"question_id":"8B.5","issue_type":"misleading_weight","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0051-E002","BATCH-0055-E004","BATCH-0057-E003"],"explanation":"Prescribed reporting and intergovernmental mechanisms can be mistaken for verified territorial compliance and milestone completion."},{"question_id":"8B.6","issue_type":"period_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E003","BATCH-0051-E003","BATCH-0032-E002"],"explanation":"Several outcomes and evaluations precede or extend beyond 2023; they require explicit temporal qualification rather than direct end-period attribution."},{"question_id":"8B.7","issue_type":"unsupported_claim","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E002","BATCH-0050-E003","BATCH-0051-E013"],"explanation":"Improved poverty, income, or coverage indicators do not by themselves establish movement caused by the ruler toward frozen goals; pandemic recovery, remittances, wage policy, and other causes remain material."},{"question_id":"8B.8","issue_type":"attribution_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0052-E020","BATCH-0054-E005","BATCH-0057-E017"],"explanation":"World Bank, CONEVAL, agency, or partner redesigns are not automatically presidential adaptation, and formal monitoring rules do not prove that failures informed ruler-directed correction."},{"question_id":"8B.9","issue_type":"attribution_error","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0052-E015","BATCH-0052-E025","BATCH-0050-E010"],"explanation":"Financial stabilization, emergency response, and institutional crisis actions involved collective authorities and external actors; personal presidential control and causal effects are not uniform."},{"question_id":"8B.10","issue_type":"misleading_weight","evidence_ids":["BATCH-0051-E001","BATCH-0052-E016","BATCH-0055-E003"],"explanation":"Durable budgets, institutions, and outputs should not be equated with durable achievement; several were newly established, contested, fragile, or not linked to outcomes."}],"overall_assessment":"Across shards, the drafts correctly identify mixed execution but sometimes give formal architecture, administrative scale, official or partner reporting, and lagged national outcomes more weight than independently verified, personally attributable implementation and durable goal progress. The corrected answers retain positive delivery evidence while narrowing causal and temporal claims, distinguishing allegations from findings, and reopening unresolved whole-portfolio, adaptation, and durability questions."},"corrected_answers":[{"question_id":"8B.1","answer":"The supplied evidence supports a mostly explicit but internally conflicted program centered on austerity and anti-corruption, poverty reduction and transfers, state-led development and infrastructure, energy and food self-sufficiency, pacification and security, and expanded military or state roles. Campaign platforms, plans, speeches, budgets, and formal strategies make major themes identifiable, but the shards do not establish one complete dated hierarchy of goals for 2023 or fully resolve changing commitments such as demilitarization versus militarization.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0051-E011","BATCH-0051-E012","BATCH-0037-E003","BATCH-0024-E001","BATCH-0055-E002","BATCH-0055-E015"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0038-E006","BATCH-0026-E010","BATCH-0051-E023","BATCH-0052-E002"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Program breadth and priority ordering remain unresolved.","Some objectives are administrative or institutional and cannot be assigned solely to López Obrador without further evidence."],"corrections_made":["Reduced certainty from fully clear to mostly explicit.","Separated stated themes from a frozen, ruler-owned portfolio.","Preserved contradictory security and institutional priorities."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A dated 2023 program portfolio is material to judging later execution.","The ledger should distinguish personal commitments from administration-wide or institutional goals."]},{"question_id":"8B.2","answer":"Major priorities were translated into budgets, laws, institutions, operating rules, appointments, programs, and infrastructure, including social-program machinery, health federalization, labor and pension reforms, National Guard arrangements, military administration of selected functions, and energy measures. This translation was selective and uneven: some measures remained proposals, lacked clear objectives or controls, depended on other institutions, or were legally constrained or invalidated. Formal enactment therefore establishes operationalization, not successful execution.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E002","BATCH-0050-E004","BATCH-0051-E001","BATCH-0051-E002","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0026-E014","BATCH-0055-E003","BATCH-0055-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E014","BATCH-0051-E013","BATCH-0051-E023","BATCH-0055-E006","BATCH-0055-E008","BATCH-0030-E005"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The complete legislative, budgetary, and appointment chain is absent.","Presidential direction is not established for every ministry, agency, Congress, or subnational measure."],"corrections_made":["Separated formal translation from execution.","Narrowed personal attribution.","Retained legal and institutional contrary evidence."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A complete program-to-law crosswalk would materially clarify ownership and implementation responsibility."]},{"question_id":"8B.3","answer":"The administration mobilized substantial resources and networks toward social transfers, health administration, infrastructure, energy, security, and military or National Guard functions. The evidence is strongest for budgets, staffing, formal structures, and deployments, but those do not prove effective mobilization toward the full portfolio. Centralization, austerity, weak monitoring, procurement risks, civilian-capacity losses, uneven intergovernmental coordination, and dependence on agencies, partners, subnational governments, or the military qualify the conclusion.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E002","BATCH-0051-E015","BATCH-0051-E016","BATCH-0041-E002","BATCH-0055-E007","BATCH-0026-E005","BATCH-0032-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E009","BATCH-0051-E019","BATCH-0047-E013","BATCH-0030-E011","BATCH-0052-E020"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No whole-portfolio mobilization record links resources to frozen objectives and results.","Institutional and military activity cannot automatically be attributed to the ruler personally."],"corrections_made":["Downgraded resource scale as proof of effectiveness.","Added source-dependence and shared-attribution controls.","Preserved evidence of broad mobilization and material constraints."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Program-level expenditure and execution records are needed to test whether mobilization was effective rather than merely extensive."]},{"question_id":"8B.4","answer":"There is evidence of active personnel management, staffing, training, and some replacement, including senior appointments, agency changes, social-program field networks, health supervisory structures, and National Guard recruitment and training. But the record does not establish systematic selection of capable implementers across the portfolio. Delayed appointments, shortages, impaired institutions, military assignment to civilian tasks, and concerns about loyalty or political alignment qualify the positive evidence, while individual presidential attribution remains limited.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0039-E001","BATCH-0044-E005","BATCH-0050-E002","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0055-E009","BATCH-0055-E010"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0051-E019","BATCH-0048-E015","BATCH-0055-E008","BATCH-0047-E010","BATCH-0026-E006"],"limitations_and_gaps":["There is no comprehensive appointment, retention, dismissal, or performance record.","Formal training does not establish practical competence or successful execution."],"corrections_made":["Removed implication that appointments demonstrated capability.","Distinguished personnel systems from individual presidential choices and results.","Qualified loyalty and expertise claims as analytical concerns where appropriate."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Named appointment chains and performance records would materially affect this lens."]},{"question_id":"8B.5","answer":"Coordination and reach were demonstrated in selected social, health, infrastructure, security, party, and emergency systems through regional structures, reporting requirements, interagency mechanisms, and nationwide deployments. However, verified compliance and milestone completion were uneven or absent in many areas: local capacity varied, coverage was incomplete, forensic and archival systems malfunctioned, autonomous bodies were impaired, and institutional resistance persisted. Formal coordination arrangements should not be treated as completed territorial control.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0051-E002","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0052-E015","BATCH-0055-E004","BATCH-0057-E003","BATCH-0029-E007","BATCH-0013-E001"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E015","BATCH-0049-E005","BATCH-0031-E019","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0057-E001"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No comprehensive regional or ministry-level compliance dataset is supplied.","Some coordination was partner-led, statutory, or institutionally collective rather than presidentially controlled."],"corrections_made":["Separated prescribed mechanisms from verified coordination.","Reduced inference from national deployments to territorial compliance.","Retained documented failures and institutional resistance."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Milestone, compliance, and regional implementation records are needed to resolve the breadth of coordination."]},{"question_id":"8B.6","answer":"Many policies became observable practice: transfers and pensions were delivered, labor and tax measures operated, health and social systems issued rules, security and infrastructure functions were performed, and major projects advanced. Delivery was nonetheless mixed. Medication and health-access problems, weak results measurement, incomplete or costly infrastructure, environmental and legal disputes, cancelled or scaled-down projects, persistent impunity, and invalidated provisions show that formal implementation and outputs did not consistently become effective, durable practice.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E002","BATCH-0050-E004","BATCH-0051-E002","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0052-E016","BATCH-0055-E003","BATCH-0044-E011","BATCH-0031-E008"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E005","BATCH-0050-E015","BATCH-0048-E009","BATCH-0030-E004","BATCH-0031-E013","BATCH-0055-E006"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The evidence is sectoral and does not establish nationwide service quality.","Several indicators are cumulative, lagged, formally prescribed, or jointly produced."],"corrections_made":["Distinguished observable output from effective service or enforcement.","Added period and source dependence qualifications.","Retained both concrete delivery and implementation failures."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Independent 2023 service-quality and enforcement audits are needed for major programs."]},{"question_id":"8B.7","answer":"Progress toward the identified goals was mixed. Social transfers, wage policy, poverty measures, pension reach, and some income or inclusion indicators moved favorably, while health access, medicine availability, education, extreme poverty, regional inequality, violence, impunity, security capacity, energy performance, and infrastructure indicators remained adverse or unresolved. The favorable results cannot be assigned wholly to López Obrador because pandemic recovery, remittances, wage changes, inherited conditions, criminal actors, subnational action, external trends, and measurement choices remain plausible contributors.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E002","BATCH-0032-E004","BATCH-0050-E003","BATCH-0050-E004","BATCH-0051-E013","BATCH-0052-E016","BATCH-0054-E003"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0032-E003","BATCH-0050-E005","BATCH-0051-E014","BATCH-0051-E017","BATCH-0048-E012","BATCH-0055-E017"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most outcomes are lagged or end before the period’s close.","There is no complete counterfactual decomposing presidential action from shocks, inherited trends, and joint implementation."],"corrections_made":["Reduced causal language around favorable outcomes.","Separated direction of indicators from achievement of ruler-owned goals.","Preserved adverse and unresolved outcomes."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A complete baseline-to-end-period counterfactual is material to this lens and is not settled by the shards."]},{"question_id":"8B.8","answer":"Some adaptation occurred through program redesign, institutional transitions, route and personnel changes, revised results frameworks, monitoring systems, emergency mechanisms, and altered lending or implementation arrangements. Yet direct evidence that López Obrador personally used audits or failures to replace implementers, reallocate resources, or improve methods is sparse. Recommendations were sometimes disregarded, weak indicators and controls persisted, and contested approaches continued despite adverse evidence. Adaptation is therefore documented mainly at institutional or program level, not reliably as ruler-directed learning.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0051-E003","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0044-E005","BATCH-0052-E020","BATCH-0054-E005","BATCH-0057-E017"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0051-E023","BATCH-0052-E002","BATCH-0050-E015","BATCH-0055-E008","BATCH-0030-E011"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Agency, partner, and court actions cannot be treated as presidential adaptation without an attribution chain.","The shards do not establish whether adaptations improved outcomes."],"corrections_made":["Narrowed adaptation from institutional change to ruler-directed correction.","Removed unsupported implications about motives and learning.","Retained evidence of redesign and persistent failure."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Audit-to-decision records linking diagnosed failure to presidential action are a material unresolved gap."]},{"question_id":"8B.9","answer":"Crisis and resistance management preserved selected priorities through social and financial stabilization, emergency mobilization, infrastructure and security continuation, legal strategies, and expanded institutional arrangements. It was mixed overall: courts constrained or invalidated major measures, the Culiacán operation failed, disaster recovery and protection were incomplete, health-transition problems persisted, military responses remained contested, and institutional resistance or noncooperation was not consistently overcome. Advocacy, journalistic, and allegation-based claims remain qualified and do not establish personal intent by themselves.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0052-E015","BATCH-0052-E025","BATCH-0050-E010","BATCH-0052-E010","BATCH-0055-E002","BATCH-0044-E009","BATCH-0029-E003"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0055-E006","BATCH-0055-E008","BATCH-0016-E004","BATCH-0031-E003","BATCH-0047-E013","BATCH-0051-E020"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Collective authorities and external actors substantially shaped several responses.","Long-term recovery, legal consequences, and international outcomes are incompletely observed."],"corrections_made":["Separated crisis continuity from successful advancement of objectives.","Narrowed personal attribution for collective responses.","Explicitly quarantined allegations and contested reporting."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Complete decision and outcome records for major crises would materially clarify effectiveness and attribution."]},{"question_id":"8B.10","answer":"By the end of the supplied period, substantial parts of the program had become budgets, transfer systems, operating rules, labor and pension measures, military and National Guard roles, administrative structures, and infrastructure commitments. This did not establish broad durable achievement: health and education capacity weakened, security and energy objectives remained unresolved, projects had cost, environmental, legal, or operational weaknesses, measurement and oversight were deficient, and some institutional changes were invalidated or dependent on personal or military control. Long-term durability and successor-period effects remain unresolved.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E004","BATCH-0051-E001","BATCH-0051-E002","BATCH-0051-E004","BATCH-0052-E014","BATCH-0052-E016","BATCH-0055-E003","BATCH-0049-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0050-E005","BATCH-0051-E014","BATCH-0051-E017","BATCH-0052-E020","BATCH-0055-E006","BATCH-0055-E008","BATCH-0030-E005"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The evidence does not cover every material program component or establish a complete start-versus-end comparison.","Durability beyond 2023, fiscal sustainability, and ruler-attributable outcomes remain unverified."],"corrections_made":["Separated durable architecture from durable achievement.","Removed reliance on survival, scale, or formal institutions alone.","Added successor-period and fiscal-sustainability gaps."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Post-period evidence and a complete end-state comparison are material to judging durability."]}]}
